name: Jesse Michaels
description: Jesse Michaels is an American singer, songwriter, and artist, most recognized as the co-founder and lead vocalist of the ska-punk band Operation Ivy. He was responsible for the band's energetic and politically charged lyrics on their sole album, *Energy* (1989). Following Operation Ivy's breakup, Michaels remained active in the music scene, forming the ska-punk group Common Rider in 1999 and engaging in other punk-related projects. In addition to his musical contributions, he is also a respected artist within the punk community, creating illustrations and paintings for albums and zines.

name: Tim Armstrong
description: Timothy Ross Armstrong (born Nov 25, 1965) is an American musician, songwriter, and record producer. He is best known as the co-founder, lead singer and guitarist of the punk rock band Rancid and a founding member of the rap-rock group Transplants. Armstrong previously played in the influential East Bay ska punk band Operation Ivy. In 1997 he co-founded Hellcat Records (a subsidiary of Epitaph Records) with Brett Gurewitz. He co-wrote Jimmy Cliff’s 2012 reggae album Rebirth, which won a Grammy. He remains an active member of Rancid, which has released ten studio albums and sold millions of records worldwide.

name: Matt Freeman
description: Matt Freeman (born April 23, 1966) is an American bassist and songwriter, best known as the co-founder and longtime bassist of the punk rock band Rancid. He and vocalist Tim Armstrong played together in East Bay bands including the ska-punk pioneers Operation Ivy before forming Rancid in 1991. Rancid’s success in the 1990s helped revive mainstream interest in punk rock, and the band has released ten studio albums. Freeman also leads the side project Devil’s Brigade (as singer and bassist). His playing, noted for fast, aggressive walking bass lines, earned him praise as 'one of punk’s most iconic bassists'.

name: Dave Mello
description: Dave Mello (born Feb 24, 1969) is an American drummer and songwriter, known primarily for his work with the hardcore ska-punk band Operation Ivy. He served as Operation Ivy’s drummer from the band’s formation in 1987 through their breakup in 1989. After the split, Mello and his brother Pat formed the punk band Downfall, while his former bandmates Tim Armstrong and Matt Freeman formed Rancid. He later co-founded the punk band Schlong. Mello remains active in the East Bay music scene, frequently performing with local bands at the 924 Gilman Street venue.

name: Lars Frederiksen
description: Lars Erik Frederiksen (born Aug 30, 1971) is an American punk rock musician and producer. He is best known as guitarist and co-vocalist of the band Rancid. Frederiksen joined Rancid in 1993 and first appeared on their second album Let’s Go. He also fronts the street-punk band Lars Frederiksen and the Bastards, and plays in the ska-punk group Old Firm Casuals. In addition to performing, he has produced records for other punk bands (for example Dropkick Murphys). A California native, Frederiksen has been a prominent figure in punk since the early 1990s. He was also briefly a member of UK Subs in 1991.

name: Branden Steineckert
description: Branden Steineckert (born April 21, 1978) is an American drummer and songwriter. He is known as the drummer for the punk rock band Rancid. Steineckert was also a founding member and the original drummer of the post-hardcore band The Used. In 2006 he joined Rancid, replacing the band's longtime drummer Brett Reed, and has recorded multiple albums with the band, including Let the Dominoes Fall (2009). Steineckert grew up in Idaho and remains an active member of Rancid.

name: Brett Reed
description: Brett Reed (born July 12, 1972) is an American drummer best known as the original drummer of the punk band Rancid. He joined Rancid in 1991 (as Tim Armstrong’s roommate) and played on the band’s first five albums. In 2002 he joined bandmates Tim Armstrong and Matt Freeman in the side project Devil’s Brigade. Reed left Rancid in 2006 after 15 years of membership. He is noted for his tight, straightforward punk drumming on Rancid’s early records.

name: Mark Hoppus
description: Mark Allan Hoppus (born March 15, 1972) is an American musician, singer, and songwriter, best known as the bassist and co-vocalist of the pop-punk band Blink-182. He co-founded Blink-182 in 1992 and has appeared on every Blink-182 album. The band broke into the mainstream with hits like “All the Small Things” from Enema of the State (1999). After Blink-182’s hiatus in 2005, Hoppus co-founded the alternative rock band +44. Blink-182 reunited in 2009 and continue to record and tour. Outside of performing, Hoppus has produced records for other rock bands and co-founded clothing brands (Atticus, HiMyNameIsMark).

name: Tom DeLonge
description: Tom DeLonge (born Dec 13, 1975) is an American musician, songwriter, and entrepreneur. He is co-founder, guitarist, and co-lead vocalist of the pop-punk band Blink-182. DeLonge formed Blink-182 in 1992 with Mark Hoppus and Scott Raynor, and co-wrote many of the band’s hit songs. After Blink-182’s initial breakup in 2005, he founded the alternative rock project Angels & Airwaves in 2005. Blink-182 reunited in 2009, and DeLonge performed on two more albums before departing again in 2015. In recent years he has pursued filmmaking and founded the media company To the Stars, which researches UFO phenomena.

name: Travis Barker
description: Travis Barker (born Nov 14, 1975) is an American drummer and producer, widely known for his work in rock and punk. He has been the drummer for Blink-182 since 1998. Barker also co-founded the rock group +44 and has played in bands like Transplants and Box Car Racer. His versatile, high-energy drumming – blending punk, hip-hop and metal influences – earned him the nickname “punk’s first superstar drummer”. Barker survived a 2008 private jet crash that killed his friend DJ AM and returned to music, later releasing solo work and collaborating across genres.

name: Scott Raynor
description: Scott Raynor (born May 23, 1978) is an American musician, known as the founding drummer of Blink-182. He joined Blink-182 at age 14 in 1992 and played on the band’s early releases, including the demo Buddha (1994), and albums Cheshire Cat (1995) and Dude Ranch (1997). Raynor left Blink-182 in 1998 and was replaced by Travis Barker. After Blink-182, he played with other punk bands and later became a police officer in San Diego.

name: Matt Skiba
description: Matt Skiba (born Feb 24, 1976) is an American musician known as the lead singer, guitarist, and songwriter of the punk band Alkaline Trio. He co-founded Alkaline Trio in 1996 and has released ten albums with the band. Skiba also served as co-lead vocalist and guitarist for Blink-182 from 2015 to 2022, appearing on the albums California (2016) and Nine (2019). In addition, he led side projects such as Heavens and his solo backing band the Sekrets. Skiba’s lyrics often mix punk energy with dark, emotional themes.

name: David Kennedy
description: David Kennedy is an American guitarist known for his work with rock band Angels & Airwaves. He joined Angels & Airwaves in 2005 as lead guitarist and has appeared on all their albums. Earlier he played guitar in San Diego punk and hardcore bands including Hazen Street and Box Car Racer.

name: Ilan Rubin
description: Ilan Rubin (born 1988) is an American multi-instrumentalist and drummer. He joined Nine Inch Nails in 2008 and has been their touring drummer and songwriter since, helping the band earn a Rock Hall induction in 2020. In 2011 he became the drummer for Angels & Airwaves. Earlier he played drums for pop-punk band Fenix TX and Welsh rock band Lostprophets. Rubin also records solo material under the name The New Regime.

name: Matt Rubano
description: Matt Rubano is an American bassist and songwriter. He first gained recognition as the bassist for emo rock band Taking Back Sunday (2003–2010), appearing on albums including Where You Want to Be. In 2019 Rubano joined Angels & Airwaves as their bassist, recording on their later albums. He has songwriting credits from his time with Taking Back Sunday and continues touring with both bands.

name: Atom Willard
description: Atom Willard (born 1973) is an American drummer known for his work with punk and rock bands. He was the founding drummer of Angels & Airwaves (2005–2011) and earlier drummed for Rocket from the Crypt (1990–2000) and The Offspring (2003–2007). He later played with Social Distortion and was the drummer for Against Me! (2013–2020). Willard’s powerful style bridges hardcore punk and alternative rock.

name: Ryan Sinn
description: Ryan Sinn is an American bassist best known for his work with punk band The Distillers. He played bass on The Distillers’ second and third albums (2003–2005). In 2005 Sinn joined Angels & Airwaves as bassist and recorded on their debut album. He left Angels & Airwaves in 2007 and later rejoined The Distillers when they reunited in 2018.

name: Matt Wachter
description: Matt Wachter (born 1976) is an American bassist and keyboardist. He played bass and synth guitar for Thirty Seconds to Mars from 2001 to 2007, appearing on their early albums. In 2007 he joined Angels & Airwaves as bassist, contributing to albums like I-Empire and Love. Wachter remained with Angels & Airwaves until 2014, after which he retired from music.

name: Eddie Breckenridge
description: Eddie Breckenridge (born 1976) is an American bassist and founding member of rock band Thrice. He has played bass (and keyboards) on all of Thrice’s albums since their debut in 1998. In 2014 Breckenridge joined Angels & Airwaves for a period, appearing on the album Love: Part Two. He also formed the hardcore punk side project Less Art with his brother Riley.

name: Rob Aston
description: Robert "Skinhead Rob" Aston (born 1978) is an American rapper and vocalist. He is a founding member of rap-rock band Transplants, serving as co-vocalist with Tim Armstrong and Travis Barker. Aston is also the lead singer of D-beat punk band Death March and was part of hip-hop trio Expensive Taste. His style blends punk rock energy with hip-hop vocals.

name: Kevin Bivona
description: Kevin Bivona (born 1981) is an American musician and producer. He is the guitarist and keyboardist of ska-punk band The Interrupters, which he co-founded in 2011 with twin brothers. Bivona worked closely with Rancid’s Tim Armstrong, playing in Armstrong’s side projects and serving as a live touring guitarist. He has produced and engineered records for various punk acts and toured with other ska and punk bands.

name: Dan Andriano
aliases: Dan Andriano in the Emergency Room
description: Dan Andriano (born 1977) is an American musician best known as co-lead singer and bassist of punk rock band Alkaline Trio. He joined Alkaline Trio in 1997 and has appeared on all their albums, providing melodic bass lines and vocals. Outside the band, Andriano records solo music as "Dan Andriano in the Emergency Room" and has toured with acts like Chuck Ragan.

name: Rob Doran
description: Rob Doran is an American bassist, notable for being the original bass player and backing vocalist of punk band Alkaline Trio. He played on the band’s early EP and their debut album Goddamnit! (1998). Doran left Alkaline Trio in 1997 to finish college and did not record with later lineups.

name: Glenn Porter
description: Glenn Porter is an American drummer known for his role in punk band Alkaline Trio. He was the band’s drummer from 1996 to 2000 and performed on their first two albums, Goddamnit! (1998) and Maybe I’ll Catch Fire (2000). Porter left the band after 2000 and has not recorded with other prominent groups since.

name: Mike Felumlee
description: Mike Felumlee is an American drummer, best known for his longtime work with Chicago’s Smoking Popes. He also played drums for Alkaline Trio from 1999 to 2001, appearing on From Here to Infirmary (2001), before returning to Smoking Popes. Felumlee co-founded the indie label Double Zero Records and has played in various punk and emo acts.

name: Derek Grant
description: Derek Grant (born 1977) is an American musician, best known as the drummer of Alkaline Trio from 2001 to 2023. He joined Alkaline Trio after Mike Felumlee’s departure and performed on every album from From Here to Infirmary onward. Earlier he played with The Suicide Machines. In the 2020s he also became a member of the rock band Dead Ending.

name: Bert McCracken
description: Bert McCracken (born 1982) is an American singer and songwriter, best known as the lead vocalist of post-hardcore band The Used. He co-founded The Used in 2001 and has sung on all their albums. McCracken co-wrote hits like "The Taste of Ink" and "All That I’ve Got". He is known for his intense, emotive vocal style and energetic stage presence.

name: Jeph Howard
description: Joseph "Jeph" Howard (born 1978) is an American musician known as the bassist and backing vocalist for rock band The Used. He co-founded The Used in 2001 and has played on every album. Howard’s bass lines drive the band’s blend of emo and post-hardcore. He also occasionally plays keyboards and contributes to songwriting.

name: Dan Whitesides
description: Dan Whitesides (born 1978) is an American drummer known for playing with rock band The Used since 2006. He joined after the original drummer left and has performed on all their albums from 2007 onward. Whitesides was active in several Utah rock bands before joining The Used. His solid drumming underpins the band’s melodic hard rock sound.

name: Joey Bradford
description: Joey Bradford (born 1984) is an American guitarist and backing vocalist. He is the co-lead guitarist of rock band The Used, joining in 2015 after the departure of Justin Shekoski. Bradford recorded on the band’s albums Imaginary Enemy and Heartwork and contributes to their songwriting. He previously played guitar in the metal band Mercykill and also produces music.

name: Quinn Allman
description: Quinn Allman (born 1980) is an American guitarist, best known as the founding lead guitarist of rock band The Used. He co-founded the band in 2001 and played on The Used’s first six albums. Allman’s guitar work helped define the band’s post-hardcore sound. He left The Used in 2015 and later formed the band Dead American.

name: Taylor York
description: Taylor York, born in 1989, is an American guitarist and songwriter, best known as the lead guitarist of the band Paramore. He officially joined the band in 2007, becoming a core member alongside Hayley Williams. York has co-written many of Paramore's songs, including the Grammy-winning single "Ain't It Fun". He is credited with helping to broaden the band's musical style and has played on all of their albums since he joined.

name: Alex Gaskarth
description: Alex Gaskarth (born Dec 14, 1987) is an American musician, singer, and songwriter, best known as the co-founder, lead vocalist, and rhythm guitarist of the pop-punk band All Time Low. He has been the frontman of the band since its formation in 2003.

name: Jack Barakat
description: Jack Barakat (born Oct 18, 1988) is an American musician, known as the lead guitarist and backing vocalist of All Time Low. He has played with the band since 2003.

name: Rian Dawson
description: Rian Dawson (born Mar 22, 1985) is an American drummer, known as the drummer for All Time Low since the band’s formation in 2003.

description: Co-lead vocalist for Dance Hall Crashers since the band's 1989 founding. Stayed with the band through every reunion; no other bands found.

name: Karina Denike
description: Co-lead vocalist for ska-punk band Dance Hall Crashers since joining in 1990. Has also sung guest vocals with NOFX, including on 'Lori Meyers'.

name: Jason Hammon
description: Guitarist for Dance Hall Crashers since 1989 and for the short-lived 1989 ska-punk project Downfall. Currently also plays guitar in Bay Area pop-punk band Beneath You.

description: Frontman, guitarist and primary songwriter of No Use for a Name from 1987 until his death in 2012.

description: Lead guitarist of Foo Fighters since 1999; previously of No Use for a Name (1995-1999) and Me First and the Gimme Gimmes.

name: Dave Nassie
description: Guitarist for No Use for a Name (1999-2009), then Bleeding Through; earlier played with Infectious Grooves (1994-1999).

description: Original bassist of Face to Face (1991-1995), then bassist of No Use for a Name from 1996 to 2012.

description: Alex Zabolotsky is a mandolin player for Old Man Markley and the former bassist for Angel City Outcasts.

description: Punk singer and musician (The Bags); Reckoner's Candace Hansen has performed with her.

name: Andrew Ferris

name: Andy Falkous
description: Singer and guitarist in Mclusky (1996-2005) and Future of the Left (2005-present).

name: Andy Hurley

name: Andy Strachan
description: Drummer and backing vocalist for The Living End since 2002; previously played with Sydney band Pollyanna.

name: Andy Yorke
description: Singer, guitarist and leader of Oxford band Unbelievable Truth; brother of Radiohead's Thom Yorke.

name: Angus Cooke
description: Angus Cooke is a cellist, producer, and owner of Santa Barbara's Orange Whip Studios; he was a member of Bad Astronaut.

name: Beer Gut
description: Punk-scene vocalist credited on the 2015 Home Street Home studio album ("Urban Campers", "Fecal Alcohol Syndrome", "High Achievers", "Safe Words"); a contemporary review noted that Beer Gut is a stage name, not his birth name. No other biographical details are verifiable.

name: Ben Dawson
description: Drummer for Kneejerk, Million Dead and Mïngle Härde. He also drums for Palehorse and has worked with Mothlite, Queen of Swords and Armed Response Unit.

name: Ben Lloyd
description: Oxford guitarist in Frank Turner's band The Sleeping Souls since 2006 and in Dive Dive. He recorded and produced Turner's first EP and first two albums.

name: Bill Stevenson
description: Drummer and main songwriter for the Descendents and ALL; drummed for Black Flag 1981-1985; co-founded The Blasting Room studio.

name: Bill Uechi
description: Bassist of the original Save Ferris lineup (1995-2002). Later formed Starpool.

name: Billy Bouchard
description: Vocalist credited on the 2015 Home Street Home studio album, singing the roles of PD and Special Ed (including solo vocals on "Three Against Me"); an album review confirmed Billy Bouchard is his real name. No other biographical details are verifiable.

name: Brandon Landelius
description: Brandon Landelius is a guitarist for Authority Zero who played lead guitar in the Mad Caddies from 2022 to 2024.

name: Brendan Kelly
description: Guitarist and vocalist of The Lawrence Arms; creative force behind The Falcon.

name: Brian Baker
description: Founding member of Minor Threat; founded Dag Nasty in 1985; guitarist for Bad Religion since 1994.

name: Brian Mashburn
description: Guitarist and backing vocalist of the original Save Ferris lineup (1995-2002). Later formed Starpool.

name: Brooke Wilkes
description: Solo singer-songwriter whose debut CD "Never Too Late" was named one of Music Connection Magazine's Top 10 Albums of the Year and whose second album "The Vanilla Life" won Record of the Year at the Los Angeles Music Awards. She sang on the 2015 Home Street Home studio album, sharing the role of Mom with Karina Denike.

name: Cahir O'Doherty
description: Singer and guitarist who fronted Fighting With Wire and played guitar in Jetplane Landing. He now plays with New Pagans and with The Sleeping Souls on their own project.

name: Callum Green
description: Drummer for The Sleeping Souls since 2020, replacing Nigel Powell.

name: Cameron Dean
description: Co-founder and original guitarist of Million Dead; he left the band in 2004.

name: Candace Hansen
description: Musician who has performed with Alice Bag and Fatty Cakes and the Puff Pastries; a member of Jennie Cotterill's band Reckoner.

name: Carter Benson
description: Carter Benson is a guitarist who played in the Mad Caddies from 1995 to 2002 and later recorded as Sharky Towers with the project Jaws.

name: Chad Price
description: Lead singer of ALL since 1993; co-founded Drag the River in 1996; fronts A Vulture Wake.

name: Chris Cheney
description: Founding guitarist, songwriter and lead vocalist of Australian band The Living End. He released his debut solo album The Storm Before the Calm in 2022.

name: Chris Flippin
description: Chris Flippin is a guitarist and longtime member of Lagwagon.

name: Chris Rest
description: Guitarist for Lagwagon (1997-present) and for Nardcore pioneers Rich Kids on LSD.

name: Christian Jacobs
description: Christian Jacobs, known as The MC Bat Commander, is the co-founder and lead singer of The Aquabats.

name: Christie Wynn
description: Pianist and vocalist who played piano on "Monsters" and sang harmony vocals on "High Achievers" on the 2015 Home Street Home studio album (credited as Fatale #2). No other biographical details are verifiable.

name: Chuck Dukowski
description: Founding bassist of Black Flag (1977-1983); later formed SWA and the Chuck Dukowski Sextet.

name: Chuck Robertson
description: Chuck Robertson is the lead singer and rhythm guitarist of the Mad Caddies, fronting the band since its formation in 1995; he also fronts the side project Ellwood.

name: Claire Miskimmin
description: Bassist in New Pagans.

name: Colin Delaney

name: Conor McAuley

name: Craig McKean
description: Drummer for Derry band Fighting With Wire.

name: Damien Sayell

name: Dan Schmid
description: Dan Schmid is the bassist who co-founded the Cherry Poppin' Daddies and formed the piano rock trio The Visible Men with Dustin Lanker.

name: Darby Crash
description: Jan Paul Beahm, known as Darby Crash, co-founded and fronted the Los Angeles punk band the Germs. He died on December 7, 1980.

name: Darius Koski
description: Guitarist and vocalist for Swingin' Utters since 1990. Co-founded Filthy Thieving Bastards and was an early member of Re-Volts.

name: Darla Belle Burkett
description: Daughter of Fat Mike (Michael Burkett) of NOFX, credited as a vocalist on "Safe Words" on the 2015 Home Street Home studio album. She also sang backing vocals on NOFX's First Ditch Effort (2016).

name: Dave Grohl
description: Dave Grohl founded Foo Fighters after drumming for Nirvana (1990-1994) and the hardcore band Scream (1986-1990). He is also the drummer and co-founder of Them Crooked Vultures.

name: Dave Raun
description: Drummer of Lagwagon and of Me First and the Gimme Gimmes.

name: Dave Smalley
description: Lead singer of the hardcore bands DYS and Dag Nasty; sang for ALL from 1987 to 1989; later fronted Down by Law.

name: Davey Havok
description: Lead vocalist of AFI since 1991; co-founded the electronic duo Blaqk Audio and hardcore band XTRMST with Jade Puget.

name: Derrick Plourde
description: Derrick Plourde (1971-2005) was a drummer best known for Lagwagon, Bad Astronaut, the Ataris, Rich Kids on LSD and the Mad Caddies.

name: Dez Cadena
description: Singer then rhythm guitarist for Black Flag (1980-1983); guitarist for the Misfits (2001-2015).

name: Dustin Lanker
description: Dustin Ross Lanker is a keyboardist best known for his long tenure with the Cherry Poppin' Daddies, as singer-songwriter of the rock trio The Visible Men, and as a member of the Mad Caddies from 2007 to 2015.

name: Eric Zamora
description: Alto and tenor saxophonist of the original Save Ferris lineup (1995-2002). Later formed Starpool.

name: Evan Kilbourne
description: Drummer of Save Ferris (1998-2002) who joined Starpool in 2010.

name: Frank Turner
description: English folk-punk singer-songwriter and former vocalist of post-hardcore band Million Dead. His backing band is The Sleeping Souls, and he has released ten solo albums.

name: Franz Stahl
description: Franz Stahl is the guitarist of the D.C. hardcore band Scream and played guitar for Foo Fighters from 1997 to 1999.

name: Gavin Hammon
description: Drummer for Dance Hall Crashers since the band's 1990s reunion lineup. Also drums in the Bay Area pop-punk band Beneath You.

name: Graham Palmer
description: Graham Palmer is a bassist who played in the Mad Caddies from 2009 to 2022, in Ellwood, and records solo material as Kinothek.

name: Greg Ginn
description: Founder and guitarist of Black Flag; founded SST Records; led the instrumental trio Gone.

name: Greg Hetson
description: Co-founded Circle Jerks in 1979; guitarist for Bad Religion from 1984 to 2013.

name: Greg McEntee

name: Henry Rollins
description: Frontman of Black Flag (1981-1986); formed the Rollins Band in 1987; also a writer and spoken-word artist.

name: Hunter Burgan
description: Bassist of AFI since 1997; bassist in Matt Skiba and the Sekrets.

name: Jack Dalrymple
description: Guitarist for Swingin' Utters since 2006 and for the Re-Volts since their 2007 formation.

name: Jack Egglestone
description: Drummer for Mclusky from 2003 to 2005 and for Future of the Left since 2005.

name: Jade Puget
description: Guitarist of AFI since 1998; co-writer with Davey Havok and partner in Blaqk Audio and XTRMST.

name: Jamie Burchell
description: Bass player in Jetplane Landing.

name: Jamie King
description: Bassist for Derry band Fighting With Wire.

name: Jarrod Alexander
description: Punk and hardcore drummer; original drummer of Death By Stereo, played with A Static Lullaby, and toured with My Chemical Romance 2011-2013.

name: Jason Moss
description: Jason Moss is a guitarist who played in the Cherry Poppin' Daddies from 1992 to 2010 and co-founded White Hot Odyssey.

name: Jason Moulster
description: Bassist and guitarist in Oxford band Unbelievable Truth.

name: Jason Sears
description: Singer of Rich Kids on LSD; died in 2006.

name: Jen Carlson

name: Jennie Cotterill
description: Singer and guitarist who co-founded Bad Cop/Bad Cop in 2011 and left in 2022. Founded the band Reckoner in 2024.

name: Jimmy Watkins

name: Joe Piripitzi
description: Original drummer for The Living End, playing from 1994 to 1996.

name: Joe Raposo
description: Joe Raposo is the bassist of Lagwagon, joining in 2010, and played on the Jaws project Death & Taxes Volume One.

name: Joe Trohman

name: Joel Wing
description: Original bassist for the 1989 Dance Hall Crashers lineup founded by Tim Armstrong and Matt Freeman. No other bands found.

name: Joey Cape
description: Guitarist and vocalist of Lagwagon; guitarist of Me First and the Gimme Gimmes.

name: Joey Garibaldi
description: Joey Garibaldi is the washtub bassist of Old Man Markley who played bass in Youth Brigade from 2007 to 2009.

name: John Carey
description: John Carey is the singer and guitarist of Old Man Markley who also plays guitar in Youth Brigade. He sang the role of Nosmo King on the 2015 Home Street Home studio album (lead vocals on "Three String Guitar", guitar on "Fecal Alcohol Syndrome").

name: John Paul Jones
description: John Paul Jones was the bassist and keyboardist of Led Zeppelin and is a member of Them Crooked Vultures.

name: Johnny Bonnel
description: Lead vocalist for Swingin' Utters since 1988. Co-founded the folk-punk side project Filthy Thieving Bastards with Darius Koski.

name: Johnny Goetchius
description: Johnny Goetchius is a keyboardist who played with the Cherry Poppin' Daddies from 1998 to 2000 and with the Mighty Mighty Bosstones.

name: Jon Chapple
description: Bassist in Mclusky from 1997 to 2003; later formed Shooting At Unarmed Men.

name: Jon Snodgrass
description: Frontman of Armchair Martian; co-founded Drag the River with Chad Price; member of Scorpios.

name: Jose Castellanos
description: Trumpeter of the original Save Ferris lineup (1995-2000).

name: Josh Homme
description: Josh Homme is the frontman of Queens of the Stone Age and a member of the supergroup Them Crooked Vultures.

name: Julia Ruzicka
description: Bassist who played in Million Dead, Quiet Kill, Who Owns Death TV and The Idle Hearts. She has played bass in Future of the Left since 2010 and released a solo album as This Becomes Us in 2016.

name: Karl Alvarez
description: Bassist for the Descendents and ALL since 1986; also played bass in Drag the River (1997-2002).

name: Keith Buckley
description: Vocalist of Every Time I Die; sang for The Damned Things.

name: Keith Douglas
description: Keith Douglas is a trumpet player who played with the Mad Caddies from 1997 to 2016 and later joined Mariachi El Bronx.

name: Keith Morris
description: Co-founder and original singer of Black Flag; formed Circle Jerks in 1979 and the hardcore supergroup Off! in 2009.

name: Kelson Mathias
description: Former bassist and singer in Future of the Left (2005-2010), previously of Jarcrew.

name: Kira Roessler
description: Bassist for Black Flag (1983-1985); member of the bass duo Dos; later an Oscar-winning dialogue editor.

name: Kris Roe
description: Kris Roe is the singer, guitarist and founder of the pop punk band The Ataris.

name: Krist Novoselic
description: Krist Novoselic was the bassist and a founding member of Nirvana.

name: Kurt Cobain
description: Kurt Cobain was the singer, guitarist, and principal songwriter of Nirvana. He died on April 5, 1994.

name: Kyle O'Neil
description: Bassist of the Detroit pop-punk band Fireworks and a member of Jennie Cotterill's band Reckoner.

name: Lauren Patten
description: Theater actress and singer who originated the role of Jo in Jagged Little Pill on Broadway and won the Tony Award for Best Featured Actress in a Musical for the performance. She played Trashley in the Home Street Home stage production (Z Space, San Francisco, 2015) and sang on the 2015 album.

name: Lena Hall
description: Theater actress and singer who won the 2014 Tony Award for Best Featured Actress in a Musical for playing Yitzhak in Hedwig and the Angry Inch. She sang the role of The Mother on the 2015 Home Street Home studio album.

name: Linh Le
description: Bassist and vocalist who joined Bad Cop/Bad Cop in 2013, completing the band's three-part harmony lineup.

name: Marc Harismendy
description: Drummer of the original Save Ferris lineup (1995-1998).

name: Mark Bush
description: Mark Bush is a trumpet player who played with Voodoo Glow Skulls before joining the Mad Caddies from 2018 to 2022.

name: Marko DeSantis
description: Marko DeSantis (Marko 72) is the lead guitarist of Sugarcult and a member of Bad Astronaut; he formerly played in The Ataris.

name: Mary Diridon
description: Lead vocalist for the Bay Area pop-punk band Beneath You. No other bands found.

name: Matt Magnusson
description: Actor and musician best known for developing the part of Nosmo (Nosmo King) in the punk-rock musical Home Street Home; he also played Tommy DeVito in the record-breaking Jersey Boys production at the Ogunquit Playhouse. He played Nosmo in the stage production and sang on the 2015 album.

name: Matt Nasir
description: Keyboardist and multi-instrumentalist in The Sleeping Souls since 2009; guitarist in Mïngle Härde.

name: Max Huber
description: Guitarist and vocalist for Swingin' Utters from 1992 to 2002. No other bands found.

name: Mikey Weiss
description: Bassist for Dance Hall Crashers in the 1990s and the 2025 reunion. Later left music to run the electronics retailer Mikey's Hook Up.

name: Milo Aukerman
description: Lead vocalist of the Descendents; earned a PhD in biochemistry and left the band in 1987 to pursue science, returning periodically.

name: Monique Powell
description: Lead singer of Save Ferris since 1995. An opera-trained vocalist who previously sang with the band Larry.

name: Myra Gallarza
description: Drummer and backing vocalist of Bad Cop/Bad Cop since the band's founding in 2011.

name: Nate Mendel
description: Nate Mendel has been the bassist of Foo Fighters since 1995; he previously played in the emo band Sunny Day Real Estate.

name: Neil Hennessy
description: Drummer of The Lawrence Arms and The Falcon.

name: Nigel Powell
description: Former drummer of The Sleeping Souls (2006-2020); member of Oxford bands Dive Dive and Unbelievable Truth. He runs the solo project The Sad Song Co.

name: Oliver Zavala
description: Trumpeter and backing vocalist in Save Ferris (2000-2002) and later Starpool.

name: Pat Mello
description: Guitarist for the short-lived 1989 Bay Area ska-punk band Downfall.

name: Pat Smear
description: Georg Ruthenberg, known as Pat Smear, co-founded the punk band the Germs and toured with Nirvana (1993-1994) before joining Foo Fighters on guitar.

name: Paul Oxborrow
description: Bassist and vocalist for the San Francisco punk band Re-Volts. No other bands found.

name: Paul Rucker
description: Drummer for Armchair Martian and for Drag the River (1996-2005).

name: Pete Parada
description: Pete Parada drummed for Jackson United (2002-2003) and Face to Face (1998-2004); he later played for Saves the Day and The Offspring.

name: Rami Jaffee
description: Rami Jaffee is the keyboardist of Foo Fighters (touring from 2005, full member from 2016) and formerly of The Wallflowers.

name: Randy Burk
description: Drummer and recording engineer for Filthy Thieving Bastards. No other bands found.

name: Robo
description: Drummer for Black Flag (1978-1981), playing on Damaged; later drummed for the Misfits (1982-1983).

name: Rory Koff
description: Drummer for No Use for a Name from 1987 until the band ended in 2012.

name: Russ Rankin
description: Singer of Good Riddance; co-founded the melodic hardcore band Only Crime in 2003.

name: Ryan Markley
description: Ryan Markley is the former drummer of Angel City Outcasts and the washboard player after whom Old Man Markley was named.

name: Ryan O'Conner
description: Actor, writer and cabaret performer who created the role of Big John in the world premiere stage production of Home Street Home in San Francisco (also spelled Ryan O'Connor in press coverage). His film credits include School of Rock, and he sang on the 2015 Home Street Home studio album.

name: Sam Given
description: Performer who served as dance captain and played Lucious in the Home Street Home stage production; he previously appeared in the ensemble of Rent at the Hollywood Bowl. He sang harmony vocals on "Three String Guitar" on the 2015 Home Street Home studio album.

name: Sara M. Lyons
description: Collaborator with Jennie Cotterill on the collaborative audio zine Library Sciences.

name: Sascha Lazor
description: Sascha Lazor is a guitarist and banjo player who played in the Mad Caddies from 1995 to 2022 and in the 1999 side project Sweet Action.

name: Scott Ian
description: Guitarist and co-founder of Anthrax; co-founded The Damned Things in 2009.

name: Scott Owen
description: Double bassist and backing vocalist of The Living End since the band formed in 1994.

name: Scott Reynolds
description: Second vocalist of ALL (1989-1993); later worked with Stephen Egerton in the project 40Engine.

name: Scott Shiflett
description: Scott Shiflett has been the bassist of Face to Face since 1995 and played in his brother Chris's band Jackson United.

name: Sean Sellers
description: Sean Sellers is a drummer who played in the Santa Barbara ska band Sparker and in Authority Zero before drumming for the Mad Caddies from 2022 to 2026.

name: Serge Verkhovsky
description: Longtime bassist for the Bay Area pop-punk band Limp and for Year of the Fist; currently plays bass in Beneath You.

name: Shaleah Adkisson
description: Singer and actress seen on Broadway and the first national tour in Hair: The American Tribal Love-Rock Musical and off-Broadway as Joanne in the Rent revival. She played Lille in the Home Street Home stage production and sang on the 2015 album.

name: Sidra Hitching
description: Vocalist credited on "Safe Words" on the 2015 Home Street Home studio album. She also read a poem on NOFX's "Generation Z" (First Ditch Effort, 2016). No other biographical details are verifiable.

name: Soma Snakeoil
description: Writer and director (also known as Goddess Soma) who co-wrote the book of Home Street Home with Fat Mike and its lyrics with Fat Mike and Jeff Marx (Tony winner, Avenue Q). An AVN Award-winning adult film writer/director, she describes herself as a writer, director, professional dominatrix and fetish film star.

name: Spike Slawson
description: Lead singer of the punk cover supergroup Me First and the Gimme Gimmes. Former bassist for Swingin' Utters (1997-2012); now also plays in Filthy Thieving Bastards and Re-Volts.

name: Stacey Dee
description: Founding guitarist and vocalist of Bad Cop/Bad Cop. Previously played in The Angry Amputees, Compton SF, The City and Blacktop Idol, and is co-founder of the Sidewalk Project nonprofit.

name: Stephen Egerton
description: Guitarist for the Descendents and ALL since 1986; record producer and studio owner (Armstrong Records) in Tulsa, Oklahoma.

name: Steve Perry
description: Steve Perry is the singer-guitarist who founded the Cherry Poppin' Daddies in 1989 and later fronted the glam-rock band White Hot Odyssey.

name: Sven Wallwork
description: Member of the band L.A. Crimes who plays in Jennie Cotterill's band Reckoner.

name: T-Bone Willy
description: Trombonist (born Brian Williams) who joined Save Ferris from the Nuckle Brothers in 1996 and later formed Starpool.

name: Tarrant Anderson
description: Bassist for The Sleeping Souls and the Oxford band Dive Dive; previously played in punk band Dustball.

name: Taylor Hawkins
description: Taylor Hawkins was the drummer of Foo Fighters from 1997 until his death on March 25, 2022. He fronted his own band, Taylor Hawkins and the Coattail Riders.

name: Todd Mohney
description: Former guitarist of Rise Against; played guitar on The Falcon's 2004 debut EP.

name: Todd Rosenberg
description: Todd Rosenberg is the drummer of the Mad Caddies (1995-1999, 2010-2022) and of the side project Ellwood.

name: Tom Fowler
description: Guitarist who replaced Cameron Dean in Million Dead (2004-2005). He later played with Julia Ruzicka in Quiet Kill, Who Owns Death TV and The Idle Hearts.

name: Tony Lombardo
description: Original bassist of the Descendents (1979-1985); played on the Fat EP, Milo Goes to College and I Don't Want to Grow Up.

name: Travis Demsey
description: Drummer for The Living End from 1996 to 2002; he now drums for Melbourne band Double Black and works as a youth worker.
